items.topic: SLC processing creates/links player and signup
items.statement: Study link clicks come in as SLC records; a process creates a player (matched by email) and a signup if they do not exist, links repeat clicks to one signup, and fills deal, operator, partner and market from the related deal (not all filled yet).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: They're going to click on the study link on the respective person's uh uh agency site and that's going to come in as uh study link click records. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And then we have a process that uh processes this information and creates a player record if it doesn't already exist and a signup record if it doesn't already exist. And it's going to try to if if the email address already exists in the system then instead of creating it it's going to link it to the existing person. Um and same thing for the signup. If somebody clicks the same study link multiple times um it will check to see if there's an existing signup and just create uh link it to that existing one. So if there's like five, they click to five times for whatever reason, you'll see all the five clicks here. You can go in and like drill down into those clicks, but it's effectively going to be represented as a single signup. And then at the single signup, we don't have all the things filled out yet, but technically like that process will fill out the deal, the operator, the partner, and market from the related deal that it's able to look up.

items.statement: Emily said an updated timeline for future phases had been committed for this meeting. Kobi said he cannot give a definite answer yet due to unknowns, but will try to bring numbers.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: The second is like the updated timeline around the future phases kind of we we had committed / Emily Vandenberg: to coming back and understanding what that looks like in this meeting. So, just I didn't know if you'd already kind of pulled that together or if that's something we'll see / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh yeah, for the other phases, I'll need to look through the rest of the components. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um I I can give you a I don't think I can give you a definite answer yet because I think we we still have a lot of unknowns to talk through for the later phases. But um I I I'll try to bring some numbers like what what we can do when when we can expect to work off of those.

items.topic: Phase 1 then ship component at a time
items.statement: Kobi proposed: Phase 1 foundation (signup and deal configuration off spreadsheets, API feeding data) must be complete and working before shipping; after Phase 1, ship one independently shippable component at a time (e.g., redeposits next). Emily said she does not disagree with the approach.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: the first focus right now is like the signup and deal configuration and everything so we can remove them from um spreadsheets uh for logging the signups uh you know make sure the API is feeding all the data in. I think that's a pretty big milestone and then from there we can start adding in the deposit um as like the next next project. / Kobi Kunasekaran: after phase one, we I think we can build components at a time um and basically work towards moving reps away from whatever process that the components going to solve from their current uh system into the new system. So like the redeposit tracking is a good one, right? Like I I might not be the exact next one, but let's bring everything that's required for redeposits as like the next deliverable. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah, I don't disagree with that approach

items.topic: November 1 stretch target pressure
items.statement: Emily said November 1st was set as a stretch target to wrap and a WagerTech stakeholder ('he', not named) will push on it; she asked what Jumpr needs answered to get a date.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: but I know he'll still be kind of really looking for We had said like a November, we kind of put that November 1st as like a bit of a stretch um to kind of wrap, / Emily Vandenberg: but he was looking you guys just kind of had mentioned a couple weeks to get it more refined and so I just know that / Emily Vandenberg: he'll be kind of coming back to that. Um, / Emily Vandenberg: as close as we can kind of get or like when what do you need answered to be able to kind of get that?

items.topic: On track for UAT end of July
items.statement: Kobi confirmed the team is on track for Phase 1 UAT by the end of July.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Um, are we still feeling like we'll be we're on track for UAT testing by the end of July or phase one? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Kobi Kunasekaran: we're able to get all this done. So, 100%

items.topic: Reps/managers can also be players
items.statement: Anyone can be a player; players are keyed by unique email. Reps and managers who need assignment or ownership must also be Salesforce user records; nothing stops them from also being players or referrers.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: I just want to ensure that we're set up in a way that a manager can be a player, a rep can be a player, and that they can like exist in that player. / Kobi Kunasekaran: to set the ownership and everything. So, anybody that needs to be assigned as like a rep uh or sales manager or anything, they they have to be like a uh like a user record as well. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um but outside of that, uh nothing stopping them from also being a player or refer or anything else. / Emily Vandenberg: Okay. Okay, that makes sense.

items.topic: Optional flag for players who are users
items.statement: Kobi offered to add a flag on players who are also users, if wanted.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So do you want players that are users to be like flagged in the system as uh players that are users? Um we can add that in if you want.

items.topic: BA assistant logins: unique vs shared
items.statement: Unique logins for BA assistants (even with lower permissions, for audit) are ideal, but depend on how many users WagerTech's current Salesforce agreement allows; Joyce expects shared logins. User count needs scoping; agreement details to be discussed with Lina.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: for BA assistants in a world where that there's people that are assisting the reps, do we want them to just use shared login or are you hoping to have unique but a relationship? / Joyce Kiddell: Uh, I mean unique would be great, but um I think it comes down to cost, right? Like I don't we need to scope out exactly how many users we're going to need internally, like excluding them and then understand if there's any left over like based off of our current agreement. Like I don't think we're going to have / Joyce Kiddell: like the ideal state is that they have their own login even if it's like a lower permission level just from like an audit perspective so we can see like what they've done in the system but um I don't think that's possible so like let's you mean Lena talk about like the agreement details Listen.
items.asr_note: Lena = Lina [ASR?]; line 647 is garbled ASR

items.topic: External proof upload, push reference via API
items.statement: Emily asked about uploading proofs outside Salesforce and pushing a reference back. Kobi said yes: the external system sends the signup ID with proof URLs to URL fields via API, which check the proof checkboxes and drive signup completion; little build if WagerTech does the processing, more if Jumpr must map raw data.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: So question we had or straw had was like is the option of like doing the upload outside of Salesforce and then pushing like reference um like a reference data point back to Salesforce something we could do relatively easily. / Kobi Kunasekaran: we could also have URL fields like three URL fields and um you could update those fields through the API from external system to fill that in and we could have it so that when that's filled the respective checkbox is checked that will drive the proof completion that will then drive the signup completion. So yes absolutely we can do that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But if you're doing all of that uh externally and you're you have the signup ID, like the exact signup that you're sending the proofs for and you're sending it directly there, then I don't think there's like anything else besides just adding the fields for you to fill / Kobi Kunasekaran: out.

items.topic: WagerTech to settle storage approach
items.statement: Emily said WagerTech will take the external storage option away and work to land it; not yet decided.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: Okay, that was that's good. We'll take that away. We're not quite there, but we'll work to kind of like land this a bit more.

items.topic: Rep-to-player comes from PlayCan payload (assumed)
items.statement: Kobi assumes the rep assignment to the player comes from the PlayCan API payload (rep ID, person info, book ID) via the SLC and is stored at the signup; he said the rep ID should be sent instead of the name.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh so my assumption is that it's actually coming / Kobi Kunasekaran: from yeah play can um from the API uh payloads that it was sending there was the player external ID or I think it was sending the name but I you should be able to send the ID instead of the name. / Kobi Kunasekaran: if not then we'll create a new one and then tie the player and the rep and everything based on that API payload / Emily Vandenberg: Okay, perfect. So it lives at the sign up and then it's coming in.

items.topic: Book ID mapping to deal or assignment
items.statement: Open: whether the payload's book ID maps to a deal, a deal assignment or a deal rep assignment; may need to be broken out if more granular.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and it had the book ID as well. I just I wasn't sure if the book maps to like a deal assignment or deal rep assignment or a deal. Uh, those we'll have to break it out if if it's going to be more granular info.

items.topic: Optional story: create player via API first
items.statement: Optional story: PlayCan calls Salesforce to create the player first and stores the returned player ID; SLC processing still keeps player info as a backfill for race conditions and out-of-order calls. That work is on the website side with WagerTech's developer.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. So there there is an optional story where instead of um us creating the players / Kobi Kunasekaran: from just a study link click, you could also have an API call out from play can to create the player records directly first. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I made sure that though like this is still included like we're still processing it at this level because there are going to be cases where there's going to be race conditions API API calls uh get out of order. So we need to make sure that when we're processing the most granular piece of information which is the SLC we still have the player information otherwise we won't be able to relate it afterwards. / Kobi Kunasekaran: but if you want you can always add the other uh other story as well to send the player record directly that way you'll also be able to get the player ID and store it in play can um but yeah that's all like work on the website end so that like you'll have to work out with their developer for
